title: COBE - Computerized Oral Bagrut Exam Rubrics
source: Ministry of Education, Table of Specifications, Rubrics and Guidelines for 4 and 5 Point COBE, updated 15-09-2026 for Winter - Summer 2027 (docs/material/cobe/COBE20232024TableofSpecsANDRubrics.pdf)

parts.name: Personal Response to a Prompt
parts.timeFrame: 2-3 minutes for listening, viewing questions and answering
parts.description: A choice of two topics. The student chooses one and responds to a set of thematically related questions in detail, in ONE recording (1-2 audio files).

parts.name: Project / Bridging Project Presentation - Responding to a Prompt
parts.timeFrame: 1-2 minutes of speaking time; a minimum of one minute is required
parts.description: A set of questions about the student's project, answered in depth in ONE recording (1-2 audio files).
topics: How the project helped them understand the literary text better
Reflections on: challenges of the work
Reflections on: teamwork vs. individual work
Reflections on: finding information on the topic
Reflections on: writing up their project
Reflections on: learning and language skills
Reflections on: personal achievement and feeling

parts.name: Response to an Audio-Visual Prompt
parts.timeFrame: 4-5 minutes for viewing and answering all questions (includes listening to the questions and viewing the clip)
parts.description: One clip (a conversation, an interview, a talk, a presentation), then TWO sets of questions about what is seen and heard. Level One (25 points): basic understanding of events and content. Level Two (25 points): understanding and interpretation of content. Each set is answered in depth.
topics: Themes: formal and informal social interactions in a variety of situations
Themes: various social and/or personal dilemmas, problems, or conflicts
Themes: various formats of interaction and presentation
Themes: reacting to lectures and speeches
Questions: giving instructions and how-to guides
Questions: distinguishing and/or reacting to different perspectives
Questions: using given information for different purposes

notes: Students are asked a set of two questions (prompts) in each part.

Responses MAY include appropriate and effective use of compensation strategies: fillers, expressions, self-correction, substitution, paraphrasing, rephrasing, and hesitation (elements of natural, spontaneous speech).
Part C: answers must be based on the spoken text. Deductions may be taken from Topic Development for answers that are inaccurate and/or not based on the spoken text.
Reading from notes or any other source is strictly forbidden and will result in Hashad.
Students must not use the stop button as a pause button. At most TWO audio files per question (two files carry no deduction). Deleting erases the whole answer.
Students must answer at least one of the questions in Part C. With no recording for either question, or a completely empty recording, the student is not eligible for a grade on the exam.
